headline: England white-wash Pakistan in three-match Test series
summary: The hosts secured an 8-wicket victory in the final Test at Edgbaston, completing a clean sweep of the visiting side.
details: England secured an 8-wicket victory over Pakistan in the final Test of a three-match series, completing a white-wash of the visiting team.
Chasing a target of 130 runs, England lost two early wickets for just 2 runs thanks to a brilliant spell by Mohammad Abbas.
However, Joe Root and Jordan Cox established a crucial 128-run partnership to steer the hosts toward victory.
Joe Root remained unbeaten on 62, while Jordan Cox finished with 59 not out to seal the win.
Pakistan had previously established a 129-run lead on the fourth day, following a strong individual performance by Razaullah.
Both teams now prepare for upcoming series against Sri Lanka, with England starting their T20 series on September 15 and Pakistan beginning theirs on October 9.
caption:
A clean sweep! England dominates Pakistan in the Test series.

England secured an 8-wicket victory over Pakistan in the final Test of a three-match series, completing a white-wash of the visiting team.

Chasing a target of 130 runs, England lost two early wickets for just 2 runs thanks to a brilliant spell by Mohammad Abbas.

However, Joe Root and Jordan Cox established a crucial 128-run partnership to steer the hosts toward victory.

Joe Root remained unbeaten on 62, while Jordan Cox finished with 59 not out to seal the win.

Pakistan had previously established a 129-run lead on the fourth day, following a strong individual performance by Razaullah.

Both teams now prepare for upcoming series against Sri Lanka, with England starting their T20 series on September 15 and Pakistan beginning theirs on October 9.

headline_marked: BNP's Rizvi Ahmed warns of [[strict action against Awami League rallies]]
headline: BNP's Rizvi Ahmed warns of strict action against Awami League rallies
summary: Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi Ahmed says the banned party has no right to hold meetings or processions, as law enforcement agencies are monitoring the situation.
details: BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi Ahmed has stated that the Awami League, whose activities are banned, has no right to hold any meetings or assemblies. He warned that law enforcement agencies will take strict action against those who attempt to do so.

Speaking to reporters after a meeting of the BNP's new standing committee on Saturday night, Rizvi Ahmed emphasized that the Home Ministry is overseeing the matter and security forces are already taking measures against those organizing programs.

He noted that that several individuals have already been detained in connection with recent activities. This follows reports of a flash procession in Gulshan, Dhaka, where 24 to 25 Awami League leaders and activists were placed on remand.

The BNP meeting also discussed the upcoming by-election for the seat vacated by Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir. The party's nomination board will make a final decision on the candidate after scrutiny on September 18.
Additionally, the BNP standing committee decided to fill organizational vacancies across the country based on seniority to strengthen the party's internal structure.
caption:
No right to rallies: BNP's Rizvi Ahmed warns that the banned Awami League will face strict law enforcement action if they hold meetings.

BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi Ahmed has stated that the Awami League, whose activities are banned, has no right to hold any meetings or assemblies. He warned that law enforcement agencies will take strict action against those who attempt to do so.

Speaking to reporters after a meeting of the BNP's new standing committee on Saturday night, Rizvi Ahmed emphasized that the Home Ministry is overseeing the matter and security forces are already taking measures against those organizing programs.

He noted that that several individuals have already been detained in connection with recent activities. This follows reports of a flash procession in Gulshan, Dhaka, where 24 to 25 Awami League leaders and activists were placed on remand.

The BNP meeting also discussed the upcoming by-election for the seat vacated by Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir. The party's nomination board will make a final decision on the candidate after scrutiny on September 18.

Additionally, the BNP standing committee decided to fill organizational vacancies across the country based on seniority to strengthen the party's internal structure.
